newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Punjab chief restored in blow to Pakistan's Bhutto.
newsitem.headline: Punjab chief restored in blow to Pakistan's Bhutto.

text.p: A Pakistani court reinstated the ousted chief minister of Punjab province on Sunday in a setback for Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.

The Lahore High Court gave Manzoor Wattoo, ousted in September 1995 on Bhutto's recommendation, 10 days to demonstrate that he could command a majority in the assembly in Pakistan's most populous province.

The three-member bench said in its order that if Wattoo failed to win a vote of confidence, outgoing chief minister Arif Nakai, whose party is in Bhutto's federal governing coalition, would be returned to power in Punjab.

President Farooq Leghari, acting on Bhutto's mandatory advice, suspended Wattoo last year after a revolt by most provincial ministers. Nakai later assumed power in the fertile, central province that borders India.
Newspapers had said Wattoo's return to power would be a blow to Bhutto's government, which has been under pressure from intensifying opposition protests.

"If Wattoo becomes chief minister again, the government at the centre will have to struggle to survive," the English-language daily The News said on Sunday. "The restoration will create an atmosphere of unmitigated uncertainty."
It said Wattoo's return could stoke tension between the federal and Punjab governments, weakening Bhutto's hold on power.
But Wattoo's prospect of winning a vote of confidence was uncertain.

His faction of the Pakistan Muslim League (PML-J) has only a handful of deputies in the Punjab provincial assembly and would need the support of the main PML opposition party led by former prime minister Nawaz Sharif and other groups to survive.

Nakai's Pakistan Democratic Front (PDF) immediately moved a no-confidence motion and asked the assembly secretary to convene the legislature. It was not known when the assembly would take up the motion.
Before the court ruling, Sharif's PML had not indicated whether or not it would support Wattoo if he was reinstated.
Once Sharif's ally, Wattoo split from him in 1993 and led a provincial revolt which helped undercut then prime minister Sharif, who was dismissed by Leghari later that year.

Bhutto, who won general elections in October 1993, gave Wattoo the top political post in Punjab in exchange for his opposition to Sharif as well as his party's support for her federal government and coalitions in two other provinces.
But later Bhutto and Wattoo fell out, with her party and some of his deputies accusing Wattoo of corruption.
